humanities_role_explanation: Designed to evaluate disciplinary competence in art history, specifically testing the iconographic interpretation and identification of Christian saints based on visual attributes and the specialized Iconclass taxonomy.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Multimodal classification task pairing historical religious painting images with text prompts containing class names, detailed iconographic descriptions, and few-shot exemplars.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Single-label image classification of religious paintings representing Christian saints. The task relies on the visual recognition of characters and symbols, combined with the iconographic interpretation of attributes mapped to the Iconclass system.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: The evaluation framework is highly domain-specific, focusing exclusively on the task of Christian iconography classification.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates state-of-the-art multimodal LLMs including GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Gemini 2.5 Flash.

quantitative_metrics.note: Evaluates performance using Top-1 classification accuracy and cross-dataset prediction consistency.

published_after_march_2023.note: The preprint was published in September 2025.

summary: This study evaluates the capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs) on the single-label image classification of Christian iconography. Using subsets of the ArtDL, ICONCLASS, and Wikidata datasets, the authors benchmark zero-shot and few-shot performance under various prompt configurations, including plain labels and rich iconographic descriptions.
key_findings: General-purpose multimodal LLMs, particularly Gemini 2.5 Pro and GPT-4o, generally outperformed fine-tuned supervised ResNet50 baselines on curated datasets, peaking at over 90% accuracy on ArtDL. However, contrastive models like SigLIP-SO400M performed better on the less consistent Wikidata dataset. Enriching prompts with iconographic descriptions typically improved zero-shot accuracy, while few-shot prompting with five exemplars yielded inconsistent results and often degraded performance.
review_notes: Analysts agreed on most fields. The disagreement on dataset_size (Ciop: 3445, Cip: 3447) was resolved in favor of Ciop by recalculating the dataset splits mentioned in the text (1864 + 863 + 718 = 3445). Disagreements on analytical_tasks and relevant_asjc_areas were resolved in favor of Cip's tighter lists, dropping 'multiple_choice_qa', 'cultural_reasoning', and 'Religious Studies' to avoid strained readings, as the paper formally structures the task as image classification within art history rather than a QA or reasoning task.
facets_explanation: The benchmark derives its reference answers from existing curated metadata natively mapped to Iconclass standards across ArtDL, the ICONCLASS AI Test Set, and Wikidata. Identifying the specific Christian saints depicted requires external knowledge of iconographic traditions and symbols that are not explicitly described in the image stimulus itself. The evaluation expects a single correct class label per image—having explicitly filtered out multi-label entries featuring multiple saints—and does not discuss the possibility of diverging annotator interpretations.
